title: Hybrid windowed-prefetch iterators: cross-SDK resumable streaming and pagination contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD and requirements doc for a unified client-side iterator abstraction that combines windowed prefetching and resumable server tokens to support both streaming and paginated workloads across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Objective: reduce implementation duplication, provide deterministic resume semantics under retries and partial reads, and enable graceful downgrade to older server versions without breaking applications.
scope: In scope: SDK public surface design for Python/TS/Go, wire-level resume token acceptance and validation rules, client prefetch window algorithm (configurable), interoperability tests, docs and migration guide. Out of scope: server implementation changes beyond emitting opaque resume tokens, advanced server-side sharding logic, and new ML model-side protocols.
requirements: 1) Unified iterator API must expose a single conceptual primitive per language: Python async iterator, TS AsyncIterable + pull-based helper, Go channel-based iterator + context aware Next() method.
2) Support two modes by config: StreamingMode (continuous partial events) and PageMode (discrete full pages). Both must support resumption from a resume_token emitted by the service.

3) Deterministic resume semantics: resume_token is authoritative; client may re-request the last in-flight window, but must provide idempotency headers to avoid duplicate side-effects for write-like operations.
4) Configurable prefetch window: default = 2 concurrent windows, max = 8. Backpressure observable by consumer through metrics and optional pushback callback.
5) Compatibility: SDK must detect server capability via capability header on handshake and fall back to legacy pagination (cursor/offset) semantics automatically when resume_token not supported.
6) Retry behavior: built-in exponential backoff for transient network errors, with transparent resume using the last persisted resume_token. Developers can opt out and manage retry themselves.
7) Observability: SDK emits structured events for resume_token issuance, successful resume, failed resume, backpressure engaged, and window-fill metrics (in SDK telemetry format).
8) Deterministic ordering guarantees for StreamingMode where server promises ordered deltas per request; SDK must preserve ordering across retries.

9) Kernel edge cases: partial-read of an event must surface a recoverable error type and not automatically advance the resume token until consumer acknowledges consumption (explicit ack API in PageMode).

10) Language idiomatic ergonomics: Python should provide async for + low-level iterator.peek(), TS should provide for await...of + iterator.peek(), Go should provide Next(ctx) -> (item, err) and RewindTo(token) helper.
acceptance_criteria: API Spec: published TypeScript/Python/Go interface reference and example snippets for both StreamingMode and PageMode.

Interoperability tests: cross-language e2e harness that runs against a mock server implementing: resume_token emission, capability_negotiation header, and simulated network interruptions. All three SDKs must pass basic resume and backpressure scenarios.
Backward compatibility tests: When mock server replies without resume_token support, SDK falls back to legacy cursor-based pagination and exposes a deprecation warning via logs once per process.

Deterministic resume test: Simulate partial window delivery + client restart; after supplying the last persisted resume_token, SDK resumes without duplicating items (idempotency header present on re-request).
Telemetry: SDK emits the required structured events; test harness validates event sequence for a reconnect scenario (issued_token -> resume_attempt -> resume_success).
Performance: Default prefetch window (2) should not increase median tail latency by more than 8% on representative payloads compared to single-window baseline; documented benchmark included in PRD.
Docs & migration guide: Clear step-by-step migration path from legacy paginated iterators to new hybrid iterators including code diffs and rollback instructions.
Security: No secrets allowed in resume_token logs; tests that verify tokens are redacted in telemetry and error outputs.
SDK usage samples for JS/Python/Go included in repo docs and validated in CI snippet tests.
Design sign-off from runtime team, SDK leads for each language, and Product (Aisha).
out_of_scope: Server-side guarantees beyond emitting opaque tokens (e.g., global sequence numbers), offering transactional read semantics, or forcing model/service-level schema changes.
success_metrics: Reduction in user-reported resume/regression bugs for streaming endpoints by 60% after rollout (tracked via support tags).
Increase in successful automatic reconnect/resume events captured by telemetry to 95% across sample workloads.
No more than 2% of SDK users opt out of automatic retry/resume in first 90 days.
Latency impact: median SDK-side added latency <= 8% for default window under typical workloads.
notes: 2026-02-18: Initial PRD drafted. Primary trade-off: aggressive prefetching improves throughput but increases client memory and possible duplicate-handling complexity. We default to conservative window=2.

2026-02-20: Engineering clarified that server will issue opaque base64 resume tokens and will not guarantee idempotency on non-idempotent operations — SDK must surface idempotency guidance and send Idempotency-Key header when re-requesting windows.
2026-02-22: Design review — agreed to provide both low-level peek/ack primitives and high-level ergonomic iterators to support different developer mental models.
2026-02-24: Security reviewed telemetry redaction; tokens must be hashed (sha256) before being emitted in any logs or metrics. Implementation note added to SDK spec.
